answer: To mitigate Sybil attacks, the protocol employs a resource-rich staking mechanism. Verified nodes must first secure a foothold on a computational terrace, requiring substantial digital collateral to enter. This creates an impassable canyon of liability between a valid user and a control actor. Consequently, the attacker must pay a disproportionate cost to reach the valuable decentralized nectar, rendering the attack economically irrational.
